claims.text: Dashboard overview
claims.note: Tile title. The Spatial Adjust module has one routed view, the dashboard (spatial-adjust-routing.module.ts:15), laid out as map, chart and table under the toolbar.

claims.text: The four regions of the screen and what each one is telling you.
claims.note: Tile summary. The four regions are the toolbar, the map, the chart and the table. On screens 1400 px wide or narrower the layout stacks and the chart is hidden (sa-dashboard.component.less:91-103), so most tablets show three regions. That caveat is carried in the correction for dashboard-overview/3/2.

claims.text: The whole feature lives on one screen.
claims.note: The module routes to one view, the dashboard (the demo child route aside). Push, settings and the other tools open as dialogs over it (sa-main-toolbar.component.html:94-112).

claims.text: Learn what each of the four regions tells you, and which numbers are measured versus calculated.
claims.note: Measured versus calculated is shown in the table: a station not scanned today is estimated under Option 2 (spatial-adjust-course.model.ts:184-188) and drawn grey and italic with a calculator icon (sa-table-card.component.html:29-32).

claims.text: /spatialadjust
claims.note: Retyped from behaviour to navigation. The root router's path is 'spatialadjust', guarded by SpatialAdjustGuardService.

claims.text: The Spatial Adjust dashboard, at /spatialadjust.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/where/1, dashboard-overview/tile/1; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.

claims.text: No dialog open.
claims.note: The push, settings and announcement dialogs open over the dashboard from the toolbar (:94-112); the guide starts with none open.

claims.text: A Spatial Adjust account on a site with TurfRad scan data, on a desktop or tablet.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/before/1, dashboard-overview/before/2, dashboard-overview/before/4; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.

claims.text: You need a Spatial Adjust account on a site with TurfRad scan data.
claims.note: 373-1135 rev 02 (introduction, before Settings Configuration) says sites that subscribe reach Spatial Adjust by logging into IntelliDash and using the Spatial Adjust button, and to contact NSN if the link is missing. In code the route guard requires a Spatial Adjust user, meaning the user's spatialAdjust flag plus a TurfRad id (spatial-adjust-manager.service.ts:185-189), and the data load returns only areas, holes and stations that have scans (SpatialAdjustService.cs:180-211).

claims.text: Without recent scans the map and table are empty.
claims.note: Scans are requested from TurfRad for the last seven days (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2510), and only areas, holes and stations with scans are returned (:180-211). With none, map and table both show STRINGS.NO_DATA_TO_DISPLAY "No data to display" (sa-dashboard.component.html:3, :36). 373-1135 rev 02 §Table Functionality: the station view shows stations with scans in the past 7 days.

claims.text: The route is all lowercase — /spatialadjust. /spatialAdjust does not resolve and redirects to the error page.
claims.note: Retyped from prerequisite to navigation, since the router settles it and 373-1135 rev 02 does not cover URLs. Angular matches route paths case-sensitively. 'spatialadjust' is the only path for the feature, and anything else falls through to the wildcard route, which redirects to /ah-snap, the generic error page.

claims.text: The view is desktop and tablet only; phones are turned away by the route guard.
claims.note: Retyped from prerequisite to behaviour; 373-1135 rev 02 does not cover device support, and the guard settles it. The route is admitted only when the device detector reports desktop or tablet, alongside the Spatial Adjust user check (spatial-adjust-guard.service.ts:22-26). Anyone else is sent to the IntelliDash home page (:33).

claims.text: Start with the toolbar
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: Look at the left end of the toolbar, at the top of the screen.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/1/2, dashboard-overview/1/6; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: The left of the toolbar identifies where you are: site name, and a course selector that only appears when the site has more than one Lynx course.

claims.text: It shows the site name, the weather strip, and the [[AVG. VWC]], [[HIGH]] and [[LOW]] figures.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/1/3, dashboard-overview/1/6, dashboard-overview/1/7; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: It shows the site name, the weather strip, and the [[AVG.

claims.text: If there is no course list by the site name, the site has only one Lynx course.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/1/2; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: Option 1 uses no ET at all, and Option 2’s figure is calculated before the page loads.

claims.text: The weather strip reports conditions.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/1/4, dashboard-overview/verify/3; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.

claims.text: The suggestions do not come from it.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/1/4, dashboard-overview/verify/3; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: Note. The average, high and low VWC figures summarise the areas of the selected course that were scanned today, whatever the table is showing.

claims.text: Toolbar, left: site, course selector, weather strip and the course-wide moisture summary.
claims.note: Figure caption. The left-hand group holds the logo, site name, course selector, weather strip and the AVG. VWC / HIGH / LOW summary (:2-32); the right-hand group, #sa-tb-right (:33), holds Push Changes, Pushed Today and the tool buttons.

claims.text: Read the map
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: Look at the map on the left of the screen.
claims.note: The map is the first child of the flex row, so it is the left column; at 1400 px or narrower the layout stacks (sa-dashboard.component.less:91-103). Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/2/1; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: Each sprinkler of a station scanned in the past seven days is a pin.

claims.text: Each sprinkler scanned in the past seven days is a pin, and pins scanned today are filled with a band colour.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/2/2, dashboard-overview/2/3; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: A pin scanned today is coloured by its measured VWC against the four moisture bands in the legend, and a pin last scanned on an earlier day is drawn clear.

claims.text: If you see no pins, the site has no scan from the past seven days.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/before/2; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: Disabled stations stay hidden while Layers is set to Enabled Stations, the default.

claims.text: See Get fresh scan data.
claims.note: Cross-reference to the guide that explains the scan request. The toolbar button with tooltip SPATIAL_ADJUST.REQUEST_SCAN_DATA is the control that guide covers (:49-59); scans are requested from TurfRad for the last seven days (SpatialAdjustService.cs:2510).
claims.previousText: Drag the handles on the colour bar to move the band boundaries — the map recolours immediately and the change is saved to your user preferences.

claims.text: A pin that is clear was last scanned on an earlier day.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/2/3; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.

claims.text: Map with the moisture legend.
claims.note: Figure caption.

claims.text: Bands default to 0–5, 6–19, 20–30 and above 30 percent.
claims.note: With no saved bands the boundaries fall back to 5, 19 and 30, which the legend labels 0-5%, 6-19%, 20-30% and > 30%.

claims.text: Use the chart for one area at a time
claims.note: Step title. The chart follows the table's current level; inside an area it offers that area's holes.

claims.text: Open the list at the top right of the chart.
claims.note: The item selector is absolutely positioned at top 10px, right 10px of the chart (sa-dash-chart.component.less:56-62). Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/3/1; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: The chart above the table plots the areas, holes or stations you pick in its multiselect, whichever level the table is showing.

claims.text: The list holds the areas, holes or stations to plot, and the chart draws the ones you pick.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/3/2; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: On screens 1400 px wide or narrower the chart is hidden.

claims.text: If there is no chart, the screen is 1400 px wide or narrower, which hides it.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/3/3; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: Selecting a row in the table changes the chart header to that area or hole and its average moisture, so the chart and the table always describe the same thing.

claims.text: Use a wider window.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/3/3; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.

claims.text: Selecting a table row changes the chart header to match, so the chart and the table describe the same thing.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/3/4; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.

claims.text: Chart and table share a selection.
claims.note: Figure caption.

claims.text: The header reads the selected item and its average moisture.
claims.note: Retyped from calculation to behaviour: the header displays a value, it does not compute one. Name, then the average to two decimals labelled CASE_SENSITIVE.AVG_MOISTURE_ABBR "AVG. VWC".

claims.text: Work in the table
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: In the table, select a hole row.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/4/2; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: The table is a drill-down: course, then areas, then holes, then stations.

claims.text: The table lists that hole’s stations, with editable columns such as [[Target VWC]] and [[% Adj.]].
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/4/4; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: Breadcrumbs at the top left take you back up.

claims.text: If you went too far, select a name in the trail at the top left of the table to go back up.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/4/3; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: At station level you get the editable columns — Target VWC, the current and suggested adjustment side by side, your own % Adj. value, and the Enable switch.

claims.text: A grey, italic [[Avg. VWC]] with a calculator icon is modelled, not measured by a scan that day.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/4/6, dashboard-overview/4/7; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: A grey, italic [[Avg.

claims.text: Hole rows for area AP.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim editing-station-targets/1/5; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: VWC with a calculator icon means the value was estimated from the model rather than measured by a scan that day.

claims.text: Selecting one shows its stations.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim editing-station-targets/1/6; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.

claims.text: Check the counts before you leave
claims.note: Step title.

claims.text: At the right of the toolbar, read the number on [[Push Changes]].
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/5/2; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: The right of the toolbar is your work queue.

claims.text: The button shows a count, such as Push 6 Changes, and the green counter beside it shows how many went out today.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claim dashboard-overview/5/3; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: Push Changes counts the enabled stations whose % Adj. differs from what Lynx holds, edited or not, leaving out any already pushed today; the green counter beside it counts stations already pushed today.

claims.text: If [[Push Changes]] is greyed out, nothing is waiting or a push is still running.
claims.note: Evidence carried over from the earlier ledger claims dashboard-overview/5/4, dashboard-overview/5/6; the sentence was reworded for the step standard.
claims.previousText: When both are quiet, there is nothing outstanding.

claims.text: Six stations pending, six already pushed today.
claims.note: Figure caption. Sample numbers; the label is CASE_SENSITIVE.PUSH_N_CHANGES "Push {{ num }} Changes" with the counter beside it.

claims.text: With nothing pending the button is disabled.
claims.note: Disabled while nothing is pending or a push is in progress.

claims.text: The map, chart and table all show the course selected in the toolbar.
claims.note: Corrected wording, replacing the sentence the ledger marked Wrong (dashboard-overview/verify/1); docs/text-corrections.md §24 gives the claimed and actual behaviour. Verified against production at the cited lines.
claims.previousText: The map, chart and table all name the same course.

claims.text: Calculation ET under the filter tabs is the figure the calculation used.
claims.note: Calculation ET shows the newest stored ET record for the site (SpatialAdjustService.cs:346-352), the record the calculation reads (:2931, GetCurrentEtForOrgAsync :2838-2882). Before SpatialAdjust:StableEtHourLocal, configured to 11 (api/appsettings.json:149), that record is refreshed from the weather service on each read, so early in the day the label can move ahead of the value today's suggestions used. 373-1135 rev 02 §Calculation ET: updated hourly, daily calculations use the 11:00 AM value. The label is ET before the Crop Coefficient is applied, and Option 1 does not use ET at all.

claims.text: The weather strip reports current conditions separately, so do not expect the two to agree.
claims.note: The strip shows the weather overlay's daily ET; Calculation ET is the stored record the server calculates with, before the Crop Coefficient. They come from different calls and need not match.

claims.text: The station count on the All Stations tab is the number of stations in the course.
claims.note: Corrected wording, replacing the sentence the ledger marked Wrong (dashboard-overview/verify/4); docs/text-corrections.md §23 gives the claimed and actual behaviour. Verified against production at the cited lines.
claims.previousText: The station count on the All Stations tab matches the number of pins on the map.

claims.text: The map need not match it, because it draws one pin per sprinkler and by default hides disabled stations.
claims.note: Corrected wording, replacing the sentence the ledger marked Wrong (dashboard-overview/verify/4); docs/text-corrections.md §23 gives the claimed and actual behaviour. Verified against production at the cited lines.
